title: enterprise-steward-engagement-kit-and-quarterly-impact-email
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, adaptable kit for Customer Success Managers (CSMs) to brief an enterprise-level steward (executive sponsor / steward) ahead of and after quarterly business reviews. Includes a one-page update, a customer-facing quarterly recap email (short + long versions), a light renewal tracker snapshot, and a playbook checklist for escalation and next-step alignment.

Audience:
Primary: Executive steward (VP+/C-level partner)
Secondary: Product/Platform stakeholders inside Redwood, internal sales exec (as needed).

Use notes (quick):
- Meant for customers with multi-team deployments, dedicated or private contracts, or renewal in next 6 months.
- Keep the one-pager to 1 page; use the email to surface concrete asks and timeline.
- Replace metrics with the latest console exports (link above).
- Tone: strategic, top-line, outcomes-first. Avoid operational minutiae unless requested.

1) One-Page Executive Update (Template)
[Header] Customer: <Customer Name> | Steward: <Name, title> | Quarter: Q<#> <YYYY> | Prepared by: <CSM name>

Key outcomes since last check-in:
- Outcome 1: e.g., 30% reduction in inference latency for core search path (production rollout on 2026-01-15)
- Outcome 2: e.g., 2% model-recall improvement after prompt tuning (A/B on cohort X)

Business impact (one line each):
- Revenue / ARR impact: <estimated $ or %>
- Cost savings: <estimated $ or %>
- Time-to-value: <reduced developer integration hours>

Customer health snapshot (traffic-light):
- Production availability: 99.98% (last 90 days)
- Latency P95: 380ms (target 350ms)
- Token cost/unit trend: -8% QoQ

Top wins / success stories (bullets):
- Cross-functional collaboration: launched private deployment pilot for compliance team; zero data exfiltration incidents, initial audit positive.
- Feature adoption: 60% of support flows migrated to streaming API, reducing average response time by 0.6s.

Risks / Open blockers (and mitigation):
- Risk: Burst capacity shortfall during peak promotions. Mitigation: propose 2-week dedicated burst window + reserved capacity add-on (cost estimate attached).
- Risk: Eval drift on reranker model. Mitigation: scheduled regression run weekly; Redwood Optimize will surface alerts and suggested model variant.

Asks from steward (decision/commitment needed):
- Confirm go/no-go for pilot expansion to EMEA (resource + compliance sign-off) by <date>.
- Approve $X reserved capacity for Q3 to guarantee throughput for campaign Y.

Next 90-day plan (high level):
- Month 1: Rollout canary for model variant B to 10% traffic, monitor quality via eval set A.
- Month 2: If quality stable, 50% rollout + enable prefix caching on hot keys.
- Month 3: Full rollout + start cost optimization pass (quantization + batching limits).

Owners & contacts:
- CSM: <Name> (email)
- Solutions Eng: <Name> (email)
- Account Exec: <Name> (email)

Attachments / data links:
- Latest latency/cost dashboard: <console link>
- Regression eval set & results: <confluence link>

2) Customer-Facing Quarterly Recap Email — Short (1-3 paragraphs)
Subject: Q${quarter} recap + next steps for <Customer Name>

Hi <Steward First Name>,

Quick recap from our side for Q${quarter}: we reduced P95 latency for your primary inference path by 12% and completed the private-deployment audit for the compliance team. Those two items together reduced user-facing latency and removed a key blocker for EMEA expansion.

Ask: Can you confirm whether the compliance team is ready to sign the EMEA pilot PA by <date>? If yes, we’ll schedule the provisioning and target a soft-launch in 6 weeks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you prefer a walkthrough before the QBR.

Best,
<CSM Name>

3) Customer-Facing Quarterly Recap Email — Long (detailed, for exec + stakeholders)
Subject: <Customer Name> Q${quarter} Business Recap + proposed roadmap

Hi <Steward First Name> + team,

Thanks for partnering with us this quarter. Below is a concise recap of performance, wins, and open decisions that will shape the next phase.

Top-line performance:
- Availability: 99.98% (90d). Incidents: 1 P2 (resolved, root cause: autoscaler bug) — mitigation patch deployed.
- Latency: P95 380ms (target 350ms) — primary improvement came from streaming payload optimization and prefix caching on call paths A/B.
- Cost efficiency: token/unit cost decreased ~8% QoQ due to improved batching and KV cache hit rate.

Success stories:
- Compliance pilot: Completed audit; no major findings. This unlocks private deployment in region EU-west-2.
- Developer velocity: Onboarding template reduced setup time for new feature teams from 5 days to 2 days.

Open items & asks (with recommended owners):
- EMEA pilot approval (owner: <Steward>) — decision needed by <date>.
- Capacity commitment for seasonal campaign (owner: <Account Exec>) — recommend 1.5x reserved capacity during campaign weeks.

Suggested next steps:
1) Approve pilot scope and schedule kickoff (target: 2 weeks after approval).
2) Confirm any security evidence required for regional rollout.
3) Schedule a 30-minute QBR to align cross-functional priorities (suggested dates: <date options>).

Appendix:
- Link to dashboard and playbook for on-call and escalation.
- High-level renewal snapshot (below).

Regards,
<CSM Name>

4) Renewal Tracker Snapshot (text table for quick paste into email)
| Contract | Term end | Renewal window opens | Current health | Suggested action | Owner |
| ACME-CORE | 2026-09-30 | 2026-06-01 | Green | Upsell reserved capacity + Optimize review | Account Exec |
| ACME-SEC | 2026-12-15 | 2026-09-15 | Yellow | Compliance confirmation required; propose Private pilot | CSM |

(Notes to CSM: keep the table to 2-3 lines in email; link to detailed spreadsheet in Confluence.)

5) Playbook Checklist (pre-QBR and follow-up)
Pre-QBR:
- Pull last 90-day metrics (console export).
- Run regression eval on main prompt set; flag any quality drops >2%.
- Verify audit artifacts (if private or dedicated).
- Draft one-page update and circulate to internal SE/AE for alignment 3 days before QBR.

During QBR:
- Start with outcomes and business impact (2 slides / 5 minutes).
- Surface 2 wins, 2 risks, and 1 ask.
- Agree on decision owner and date for each ask.

Post-QBR (48–72h):
- Send customer-facing recap email (short + long options) and attach one-pager.
- Create follow-up Jira tasks for each decision with owners and due dates.
- Update renewal tracker and notify AE of upsell opportunities.

6) Escalation matrix (short)
- Quality regressions: Solutions Eng -> Applied ML -> Product (priority P1 if user impact).
- Capacity incidents: SRE -> Infrastructure -> Account Exec (for customer-facing comms).

7) Example micro-templates (copy/paste)
- 20-min QBR scheduling ask (very short):
"Hi <Name>, are you available for a 20-min QBR week of <date options>? We’ll share a 1-page update and 2 decision asks. If you prefer a written recap only, we can send that instead.
"
- Approval reminder for steward (gentle):
"Hi <Name>, following up on the EMEA pilot approval. Approving will let us reserve capacity and complete provisioning ahead of your campaign window. Can you confirm by <date>?
"
8) Notes to self / CSM tips (informal)
- If steward is time-poor, send the short email and add a 1-slide visual showing ARR impact. Execs respond better to $$ impact + calendar ask.
- Keep technical deep-dives for stakeholders; execs want outcomes.
- Use the console metrics export rather than manually typing numbers to avoid mismatch.

9) Versioning & maintenance
- Owner: Maya Chen (CS Strategy)
- Next review: 2026-05-01
- Change log (top): 2026-02-28: added burst capacity play and updated latency targets.

---
End of kit.

Quick checklist before sending this to customer: replace angle-bracket placeholders, attach console report, confirm AE has sign-off on recommended financial ask.
